jobs.title: AI & Data Analytics Partner
jobs.description:
About Jimdo

We exist to unleash the power of the self-employed - helping solopreneurs and micro-businesses thrive by doing what they're passionate about and removing the complexity of building lasting, successful businesses.  Jimdo started in 2007 when three school friends built a website builder in a Northern German farmhouse to help everyone build a presence online. Today, we're a profitable, remote-first company with 220+ people from 50+ nationalities working across 15+ countries. We've helped build over 36 million websites to get online across the world.  We're more than just a website builder. We're an AI-powered platform that helps self-employed people actually run and build successful businesses — from getting found online, winning customers and running their business with a peace of mind by knowing exactly what to do next to move forward.  At the heart of Jimdo is a strong belief in personalized, data-driven guidance. Our platform combines design, business tools, and an AI-powered core that turns real customer data into clear insights and next steps helping our customers focus on what moves their business forward.

Role Overview:

Jimdo is becoming an AI-first company, and our People team is one of the first places where that shows up in daily work. We're looking for an AI & Data Analytics Partner to build the agents, analytics and workflow automations that make the People team faster, smarter and easier to scale.  You'll take a process from "this is slow and manual" to a working, compliant solution in production, and then make sure the team can run and extend it without you. You'll also give leadership one reliable view of People data, so decisions rest on numbers everyone trusts.  You’ll start with the People team, and the scope can grow to any other function across Jimdo.

The team and who you'll work with:

You'll report to the Manager Performance Intelligence and work day to day with the People team and our HR Business Partners.  You'll also work closely with our AI team on standards and capabilities, with Finance and Legal on data consistency and compliance, and with our HR system and payroll providers.  This is a remote role, open to candidates based in Germany, Italy, Spain or Portugal.

Help Us Change the Way the World Works

Build something that matters.  Langdock exists to change the way the world works, bridging the gap between what technology can do and what people actually do with it. We bring all leading AI models into one secure, model-agnostic platform and make them usable across entire organizations. Over 10,000 companies use our platform every day, from fast-growing startups to some of Europe’s largest enterprises. Their employees open Langdock to draft strategies, analyze documents, or automate workflows, helping them to work smarter, think more creatively, and reach their full potential.

About the Role

This is a full-time internship of at least 6 months at our Berlin HQ, and it is not a regular internship application. We don’t want your CV first. We want to see what you have built.  If you build with AI because you can’t stop, with Langdock, Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or anything else, show us. If your project convinces us, we shape the internship around you and your strengths.

What We Want to See

Record a Loom of something you built with AI. It should be no longer than 5 minutes. Two kinds of projects get our attention:

Something that would help Langdock. Look at our product roadmap and at our product, and build something that solves a real problem for us or our customers. That could be a feature prototype, an internal tool, a GTM engine, a support automation, an eval setup, or something we haven’t thought of yet.

A genuine passion project. Something you built because you couldn’t stop thinking about it, and that shows how you think.

What we don’t want:  basic chatbots, simple prompt wrappers, “summarize my inbox” agents, or linear three-step workflows. Our customers build those every day. Show us something that made you think hard, and that makes us think too.

What Your Loom Should Cover

The problem:  what you solved and why it matters.

The demo:  show it working live, not on slides.

How it’s built:  the models, tools, architecture, and key decisions behind it.

What broke:  where it failed and what you learned from that.

What’s next:  what you would build at Langdock if you joined.

What You Will Do

Own a real project. Ideally it’s the one you showed us. You take it from prototype to something our team or customers actually use.

Work directly with the team. You work alongside Product, Engineering, or GTM, depending on where your project lives.

Ship, measure, iterate. You present your progress regularly and decide based on real feedback.

How to Apply

Paste your Loom URL into the field “Your Build” in the application form. Your LinkedIn profile is enough; a CV is optional.

You Might Be a Fit If…

You build, not just talk about AI. You have shipped things that work, even if they’re rough.

You think in impact, not just in technology.

You show high agency. You don’t wait for tasks; you find them.

You experiment constantly with new models and tools.

We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.  We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who care about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few. We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities and growing from our offices and remotely. Join us and build a better future for our society.  In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Compliance Director and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.  You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own

Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

About Doit

We are focused on reinventing how people spend, save, invest, exchange, travel, and more. Our objective is to build tools that will help people get more from their money and become an expert at ease. We believe AI will help make finance smart, accessible and safe.  We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who love building great next-generation products, not status quo. Account Executive, Strategic Deals - Attribute™

Location
This is a fully remote opportunity based out of any of the following with travel as needed: UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Sweden, Estonia.

Who We Are
Become part of the team behind Attribute™. Following our recent acquisition, we're bringing together visionary engineers and go-to-market leaders to disrupt cloud management with real-time, tagless cost visibility across cloud and AI workloads. As an Account Executive focused on Strategic Deals, you'll join a founding GTM movement inside an established market leader trusted by over 4,500 global customers, unlocking high-impact opportunities through top-tier strategic partnerships.

DoiT empowers cloud-native organizations to scale faster and innovate with confidence. By combining our Cloud Intelligence technology with Forward Deployed Engineers and deep specialization across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, we help tech-forward companies navigate their toughest infrastructure and cost governance challenges end to end.

The Opportunity
As an Account Executive, Strategic Deals for Attribute™, you will be at the forefront of building a brand-new region from scratch and introducing a groundbreaking solution to a fundamental business problem in modern FinOps. You will work on Strategic Deals, leveraging strategic partnerships with AWS, OpenAI, Top Private Equity firms, and our global current install base. A strong focus will be placed on co-selling and unlocking strategic deal opportunities with AWS, ISVs, and channel partners. Traditional cloud cost allocation methods rely heavily on static tagging—an approach that becomes obsolete in modern, shared cloud and AI infrastructure. When multi-tenant clusters, shared GPUs, microservices, and dynamic AI workloads dominate, organizations face severe blind spots: they cannot accurately determine the true cost-to-serve for specific applications, autonomous agents, or business teams, making it impossible to calculate true gross margins at a granular customer level.

Attribute™ solves this by taking a completely different approach. Leveraging runtime eBPF technology, Attribute™ captures real-time network traffic signals and kernel-level observability without requiring engineering teams to manually tag or instrument code. By analyzing actual runtime consumption across CPU, GPU, memory, network, and AI model API requests, it provides accurate total cost of ownership (TCO) and unit economics based on real usage. Organizations finally get precise cost governance and gross margin

jobs.title: Staff Applied AI Researcher (Agentic Search)
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast-growing team building an agent-native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.

You can think of this as Google search, but for AI agents: a system designed for machines, not humans. We are building agentic search, where AI systems actively plan, retrieve, evaluate, and refine information rather than simply returning results. As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing these systems to search and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval, ranking and passage extraction under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24/7.

This role comes with ownership over key parts of our applied AI research direction and system design, with a strong expectation of defining new approaches and shipping measurable impact in production. In the first year, you will own a specific part of the search stack, e.g. ranking or iterative retrieval.

What you'll work on:

  • Designing an agent-native search system that handles everything from low-latency single-hop search to complex deep search tasks requiring iterative planning, querying, refinement and reasoning.

  • Training ranking and retrieval models optimized for agent-driven workflows under real world constraints

  • Bringing the latest advances from the research community to our search stack and ship it to production.

Your responsibilities:

  • Drive applied research and technical direction across retrieval and ranking systems

  • Design and evolve multi-stage retrieval architectures (query understanding, rewriting, retrieval, reranking and iterative retrieval)

jobs.title: Founder Talent Acquisition
jobs.description:
Who we are

Hexa is a venture studio. Since 2011, we've built more than 60 companies, including 3 unicorns. Every year, our startup studio, Hexa Start, creates 12 companies from scratch, and our accelerator, Hexa Sprint, funds several dozen more. Each Start company begins with a CEO and a CTO we recruit ourselves: finding them is our core business.  That's where you come in. 👀

The role

Our partners bring the ideas. What turns an idea into a real company is the people who build it, so finding the right founders is Hexa's core business. That's your job: convincing aspiring founders to join us, walking them through a life-changing decision, and putting them in front of the right partner at the right time.  Our marketing team builds and nurtures the reservoir of future founders. You turn it into a pipeline for each open role (say, a CTO for a cybersecurity project with experience in LLM-built attacks), run the search with the partner leading the project, assess, and close. Laure, your peer, does the same for each company's first employees.  This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll need the business sense to read an idea and know what kind of founder it calls for, and a sharp eye for entrepreneurial profiles: you can tell a true entrepreneur from a strong manager, even when both look great on paper.

What you'll actually do

Source, hands-on: inbound comes first, but you roll up your sleeves and reach out to everyone who looks on track to start something, before anyone else does,

Build a pipeline for every open founder role within two weeks, from your own sourcing, the marketing reservoir and our scoring agents,

Own the founder scorecard with the partners and fine-tune it every quarter against real hiring outcomes,

Interview, assess and close demanding, sometimes hesitant candidates, alongside partners and our CTO,

Tell marketing and community what each search is missing, down to the event it needs,

Act as product owner of our recruiting stack (Ashby, sourcing tools, AI agents), and call in agencies when a search runs short.

What we're looking for

2 to 7 years in recruiting or talent acquisition, close to founders: fast-growing startup, VC fund, accelerator, studio, or founder and executive search

You know what makes a strong founder, and you have examples rather than generalities

A track record of closing senior or founder-level candidates, with numbers to back it

You build trust fast, and you can challenge a candidate without putting them off

You're as comfortable testing an agent or optimizing a workflow as building a relationship

You have the standing to disagree with a partner, and the judgment to know when not to

You are fluent in English and French

First call with Laure, Talent Partner

Introduction call with our CEO, to deepdive on the role

Case study on a live search: pipeline, gaps and your plan for the next two weeks

Interviews with two partners

jobs.title: Responsable enquêtes & plaidoyer
jobs.description:
Green-Got est une institution financière française qui permet à chacun de choisir ce que son argent finance. Nous avons été distingués pour notre exclusion des énergies fossiles par Reclaim Finance, bank.green, Bank for Good ou encore Moralscore. Green-Got est aussi lauréat de l'Impact 40 depuis 3 années consécutives.
Depuis cinq ans, nous montrons où va l'argent. Nos membres ont sorti 300 millions d'euros des grandes banques. Notre mission est de définir de nouveaux standards pour le secteur financier, alignés avec la science, et non pas les intérêts des industries fossiles.

Pourquoi ce recrutement ?

Les banques traditionnelles ont des lobbyistes.  Ils défendent leurs profits et les industries qu'elles financent. Les citoyens, eux, n'en ont jamais eu. C'est désormais le cas.
Pendant plusieurs mois, nous avons enquêté sur le financement des pesticides par les banques françaises. Mais dénoncer ne suffit pas : la prochaine étape, c'est la loi. Nous recrutons la personne qui enquêtera à nos côtés, dévoilera ce que le système préfère laisser dans l'ombre et proposera des solutions concrètes pour changer les règles. Elle racontera chaque étape du combat à nos membres, en toute transparence.

Missions

Ton travail tient en trois verbes : enquêter, dévoiler, proposer. Tu portes 2 à 3 grandes campagnes par an, de la première piste jusqu'au texte de loi, et tu les incarnes.

1. Enquêter

Faire la  veille  de l'actualité politique, réglementaire et scientifique (Parlement européen, Assemblée nationale, comitologie, ONG), et nourrir l'équipe Média pour nos contenus réactifs.

Repérer les  sujets de nos grandes campagnes de mobilisation  et les valider avec nous : fludioxonyl, TotalEnergies financé par les Livrets A .

2. Dévoiler

Mener les recherches sur les campagnes validées. Ce n'est pas de la réaction à chaud : ce sont 2 à 3 combats de fond par an.

Creuser les rapports, les bilans et les sources primaires que personne ne lit, et en sortir des  informations inédites .

Trouver les  angles  : quelles personnes interroger (un agriculteur, une famille touchée), comment les contacter, quels contenus en tirer avec l'équipe Média.

Incarner l'enquête  pendant qu'elle se fait, face caméra et sur le terrain :

Prendre la parole  face caméra  (vidéos, lives, interventions médias) et partager régulièrement où en est le combat.

Director Service Accounts @ Sereact 🦾

Director Service Accounts (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites across Europe · Reports to the VP Operations · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.  Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

The Site Acceptance Test is where a deployment ends and a customer’s operation begins. From that day our robots pick in someone else’s building, every shift, against targets the customer measures. Many of our customers buy Sereact as a service: they pay for robots that work, not for robots that were delivered.  Our deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the site that performs is the site that grows. We now want one leader who owns every live site from SAT on: keeps it at target, brings it everything we ship in software and hardware, speaks for the customer inside Sereact, and turns a working site into a growing one.

The Real-World Learning Loop runs through your sites

Cortex learns from live deployments. Every station at a customer is part of that loop, so a station that is down is more than a service problem: a cell sitting dark is a stopped sensor.

In-Situ Policy Execution. Every live station runs the current policy in a real operation. Your surface on it: each site at target, every shift.

Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: stations that run and stay connected, so the data keeps coming.

Data Curation and Learning. Failures and edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: what your sites tell us reaches engineering and research with the context they need.

Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. Your surface on it: they land in your customers’ operations on a schedule the customer can plan around, with a way back if something is off.

A site that runs well teaches Cortex more, and it grows.

Responsibilities

Take over every site at SAT. Set the standard for what a site needs before your team takes it on: documentation, open points, spare parts, contacts and targets. If a site is not ready, it stays with deployment until it is.

Keep every site at target. Own each site’s performance against its contract: availability, throughput and pick success. See a problem coming before the customer does, and run the recovery plan when a site falls behind.

YOUR MISSION

A software engineer today uses Claude Code or Cursor. A mechanical engineer designing the next jet engine still searches Excel sheets and asks whoever has been around longest.

We are building the AI co-engineer for physical products: one that works natively in 3D and learns from real engineering decisions. We are in production with major European manufacturers, with real revenue and customers who tell us when we are slow.

The problems are open ones. Getting an agent to reason usefully about geometry, making 3D search work on real customer part libraries, and figuring out what the interface even looks like when an engineer asks why a bracket failed. There is research to borrow from and very little product to copy.

Senior or staff level depending on experience.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

You will own large problems end to end, across the stack. We cannot say exactly what that looks like in month three, but here is what the last two years have actually involved.

A multi-agent orchestration SDK ,  built from scratch . Nothing off the shelf handled what we needed: long-horizon execution that runs for hours and survives restarts.

CAD conversion as a real pipeline . It used to be manual and brittle. Turning it into production infrastructure meant writing a Python wrapper around a C++ SDK and making it reliable enough to sit under everything else.

Migrating the application off Electron and Webpack onto SSR React with Vite . That architecture is what the whole product now sits on.

What is coming:

3D-to-3D search  across real customer part libraries, not benchmark datasets

Constraint solvers and optimization , and getting an agent to use one sensibly

Agents that hold a useful model of a physical object , which is still an open problem

Hybrid cloud deployments  for manufacturers who cannot send their data anywhere

We work in Python and TypeScript, with multi-agent orchestration and AI integrations across several providers.

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

You have shipped production systems across frontend and backend, and can point at them

Your CV reads as a set of problems, not a stack

You use AI heavily to go faster, but you built things the hard way first

You are fine when the problem is not yet defined

You deliver end to end, and you are still there when it needs maintaining

jobs.title: Privacy & Product Counsel
jobs.description:
This role can be office-based in Freiburg, Germany/ San Francisco, USA or remote-first, with a requirement to be in the office one full week per month.

About Black Forest Labs

We’re the team building the foundational layer for visual intelligence: multimodal models trained jointly on images, video, audio, and action to see, generate, and understand the world.  Our founding team pioneered latent diffusion and Stable Diffusion, the breakthroughs that made generative AI accessible to millions. With FLUX, we're pushing into generative media at scale, machines that act in the physical world, and emerging applications in computer use.  Our FLUX models top public benchmarks and run in production in some of the world's biggest platforms. We're a small, fast growing research lab competing with the largest companies in the world. From our labs in Freiburg to San Francisco, we're building what comes next.

Why This Role

Every FLUX release, API feature and enterprise offering requires legal oversight. Black Forest Labs’ (BFL) frontier technologies raise questions where there is no established precedent – especially as we push further into video, perception and physical AI.  We’re hiring a Privacy & Product Counsel to find solutions and help drive our product teams forward. You’ll sit in our Legal, Policy & Assurance (LPA) team and be embedded with research, product and engineering, shaping how BFL builds and ships.  This is a hands-on role for someone who wants to build a privacy function at the frontier of AI and robotics.

What You’ll Work On

Product counselling. Be the go-to lawyer for product teams on new models, API features and innovative products, from first spec to launch, giving clear, risk-calibrated advice that keeps us shipping.

Marketing. Partner with our Growth, Marketing and DevRel teams to review launch announcements, model cards and campaign copy so that our claims about FLUX are accurate. Advise on privacy matters relating to product marketing, analytics, commercial and creator partnerships, and advertising claims.

Privacy by design. Own BFL’s GDPR programme across the model lifecycle: training data, fine-tuning, inference, logging and retention. Run point on DPIAs and privacy documentation as required.

Customer commitments. Partner with GTM on DPAs, zero-data-retention and no-training terms, security questionnaires and enterprise negotiations – and work with the team to ensure that what we promise matches what we do.

International transfers and vendors. Manage EU–US transfer mechanisms (SCCs, the EU–US Data Privacy Framework and TIAs), and run privacy diligence on sub-processors and AI tooling.

US privacy. Track and implement obligations under US state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and peers) and emerging AI-specific state legislation.

Regulatory interface. Prepare BFL for engagement with data protection authorities, and handle data subject requests, complaints and incidents, including breach assessment and notification.

Scale’s rapidly growing Global Public Sector team is focused on using AI to address critical challenges facing the public sector around the world. Our core work consists of:

jobs.description:
The Insights discipline helps empower Rioters' decision-making to be more data-informed. We're an interdisciplinary group of scientists, consultants, and strategists from all sorts of backgrounds who join together to represent and advocate for gamers around the world. We believe that illuminating the globally diverse experiences, behaviors, and needs of gamers is critical to Riot living up to our player-focused mission. We're a group united by our love of games, science, and helping others succeed.

As a Manager, Insights on the Riot Discovery Studio Insights (RDSI) team, you’ll oversee the efforts of one or more team members delivering critical insights and validation to our R&D games. You and your direct reports will conduct studies and analyses to inform the direction, experience, and systems of Riot’s future games. You will report to the research lead of RDSI and contribute to their overall efforts to lead the team and grow its capabilities. These responsibilities will include: helping to ensure the overall quality of insights delivered, supporting/driving team processes, and generating new ideas or capabilities that improve how we do research. Your research skill set, strong communication skills, and mentorship capabilities will ensure that we have a high function and efficient centralized research team that can help ensure our games have the information they need about their audience to make games in a player focused way. You will report to the Sr. Manager, Insights on the team.

jobs.title: Agent Security Engineer
jobs.description:
Belmont Lavan is hiring an Agent Security Engineer to secure autonomous AI agents before and after they reach production. Agents now call tools, hold credentials and act on live systems, so they need the controls we already expect for people and services: identity, least-privilege access, monitoring and testing.  You will sit between AI engineering and security. You will design the guardrails, attack the systems yourself, and build the governance controls that let the business deploy agents with confidence.

Requirements

5+ years in security engineering (AppSec, cloud security, IAM or offensive security), with at least 1 year securing LLM or agent-based systems  Hands-on knowledge of LLM attack techniques: prompt injection, jailbreaks, data exfiltration via tools, RAG poisoning  Experience designing identity and access controls: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, token exchange, workload identity, secrets management  Working knowledge of agent frameworks and protocols such as LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI or Model Context Protocol (MCP)  Strong coding skills in Python, plus one of Go, TypeScript or Rust  Cloud security on AWS, Azure or GCP, including logging, detection and policy-as-code (e.g. OPA / Cedar)  Ability to explain AI risk clearly to engineers, risk teams and executives

Matchmaking is a critical stage downstream of Discovery and Search. Once a player chooses a game to play, matchmaking assigns them to a server for that game. That decision shapes who they play with, the network latency they experience, and the quality of their session. By matching players to servers that fit their needs and each developer’s game, matchmaking helps turn discovery into satisfying play, repeat visits, and long-term engagement, making it a direct lever for Roblox’s growth.

As a Principal ML Engineer on Matchmaking, you’ll own the technical vision and execution for the models, objective functions, and algorithms that make those decisions. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Product Manager, Enterprise

Scale is accelerating the development of AI across the world's most important organizations. The Forward Deployed PM is the person who makes enterprise deployments succeed from the product side — embedded with customers, shaping real production outcomes, and translating messy operational reality into high-signal input for the core platform.

This is not a roadmap PM, a CSM, or a solutions engineer. The FDPM owns product outcomes inside a portfolio of enterprise accounts: earning deep trust with senior customer stakeholders, driving deployments to production, identifying where the product is the bottleneck vs. execution, and feeding durable, specific signal back to the platform team. The best FDPMs have shipped products into large organizations and can tell the difference between a customer's stated request, their actual problem, and what the platform should do.

What You'll Do

  • Own product outcomes for our highest impact enterprise accounts. You are the accountable PM for product delivery and customer value.
  • Build trusted advisory relationships with VP/C-level buyers and senior technical leads. Become the reliable escalation point on the Scale side before issues surface externally.
  • Drive deployments from contract to production. You have done this before for large organizations. You know what 'production-ready' actually means and you close the gap.
  • Translate real customer workflows, friction, and priorities into high-signal product input for core platform teams. Not requirements docs — specific, evidence-backed product perspective with tradeoffs articulated.
  • Distinguish where the product is the constraint from where execution, integration, or change management is. Drive each type of blocker to resolution through the right channel.
  • Partner closely with FDEs so the account runs as a coordinated team, not a set of parallel workstreams.
  • Identify and develop expansion opportunities grounded in demonstrated customer value
  • Represent customer reality to platform and leadership with enough credibility that it changes decisions.

What We're Looking For

  • Enterprise deployment ownership: has driven AI/ML or complex software products from contract to production at scale, with real integration, real security constraints, real change management.
  • Product judgment in the field: translates customer reality into product direction, not just feature requests; can say no credibly and explain why.
  • Customer trust-building: earns and maintains trust with demanding senior stakeholders over multi-quarter engagements; manages conflict without eroding the relationship.
  • Technical translation: bridges the gap between customer engineering teams and Scale platform engineers; does not relay messages, adds interpretation.<

The goal of a Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to leverage techniques in the fields of generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI to improve Scale's products and customer experience in production environments. Our machine learning engineers take advantage of robust internal infrastructure and unique access to massive datasets to deliver improvements to our customers.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with a strong focus on both large language models and computer vision. On the LLM side, we are developing agentic systems that help solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners. Our efforts include building large-scale fine-tuning pipelines, training models across multiple modalities, and developing generalizable vision foundation models to support a wide range of defense applications.

  • Improve and maintain production models through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
  • Collaborate with product and research teams to identify and prototype ML-driven product enhancements, including for upcoming product lines

  • Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
  • Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
  • Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

jobs.description:
About the Collective

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC)’s mission is to bring the world's best minds to shape the future of AI – because the future of AI depends not only on powerful models, but on the people who teach them to think.

jobs.title: Machine Learning Research Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA
jobs.description:
At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. Our products provide the high-quality data and full-stack technologies that power the world's leading models, and help enterprises and governments build, deploy, and oversee AI applications that deliver real impact. We work closely with industry leaders like Meta, Ernst & Young, Mayo Clinic, Time Inc., the Government of Qatar, and U.S. government agencies including the Army and Air Force.

Scale's Machine Learning Research team builds the foundation for the next generation of AI systems — pushing the boundaries of what's possible with frontier models while ensuring safety, reliability, and alignment at every step. Our work spans generative AI, reinforcement learning and advanced post-training methods, scalable oversight, synthetic data pipelines, red teaming, and evaluation science.

We are developing a large-scale hybrid human-machine system to power machine learning pipelines for dozens of industry-leading customers. These models and systems form the backbone of Scale's long-term strategy, enabling billions of tasks monthly and supporting some of the most complex and advanced use cases in the AI ecosystem.

As an intern, you'll work on a combination of deeply technical ML applications in production and cutting-edge research problems, with mentorship from world-class researchers and the opportunity to collaborate with leading teams across industry and academia. Interns own real, published or shipped work — not side projects.

Example Projects

  • Measure the dangerous capabilities of frontier models and conduct preparedness research
  • Research the science and creation of new benchmarks for frontier models
  • Develop new methods for training models to excel on extremely difficult reasoning problems that require long chains of thought
  • Research reinforcement learning and post-training methods that improve model reliability on high-stakes tasks
  • Research scalable oversight protocols that enable humans to produce and quality control reasoning chains beyond their native capabilities
  • Study the boundaries of model generalization and capabilities to inform data-driven advancements
  • Research synthetic and hybrid data with humans in the loop to scale up high-quality data generation
  • Take models currently in production, identify areas for improvement, improve them using retraining and hyperparameter searches, then deploy without regressing on core model characteristics
  • Create post-training or agentic solutions that integrate into our ability to deliver applications for enterprise and public sector clients

Required to Have

  • Currently enrolled in a BS, MS or PhD program with a focus on Machine Learning, Deep Learning, or Natural Language Processing, with a graduation date in Fall 2

jobs.title: Machine Learning Research Scientist, Evaluations

jobs.description:
Scale works with the industry's leading AI labs to provide high quality data and accelerate progress in GenAI research. We are looking for Research Scientists and Research Engineers with expertise in LLM post-training (SFT, RLHF, reward modeling) and evaluation. This role is on the evaluation pod within the GenAI Research Organization and will focus on building benchmarks and diagnosing model failure modes in both text and multimodal modalities.

In this role, you will develop rigorous evaluations and diagnostic methods that reveal where frontier models fail and why. You will collaborate with researchers and engineers to define best practices in evaluation-driven AI development. You will also partner with top foundation model labs to translate failure analysis into technical and strategic input on the next generation of generative AI models.

You will:

  • Analyze model behavior to identify, characterize, and diagnose failure modes in frontier LLMs and Agents. You’ll identify everything from capability gaps and reasoning errors to robustness and alignment issues, all focusing on RCA.
  • Design and build benchmarks and evaluation methods that measure LLM capabilities in both text and multimodal modalities.
  • Apply post-training expertise (SFT, RLHF, reward modeling) to connect observed failures to the data and training interventions that address them.
  • Publish research findings in top-tier AI conferences.

Ideally you’d have:

  • Ph.D. or Master's degree in Computer Science, Machine Learning, AI, or a related field.
  • Deep understanding of deep learning, reinforcement learning, and large-scale model fine-tuning.
  • Experience with post-training techniques such as RLHF, preference modeling, or instruction tuning, and with LLM evaluation or benchmark development.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Published research in areas of machine learning at major conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, CVPR, etc.) and/or journals.
  • Previous experience in a customer facing role.

jobs.description:
Role Summary

Scale is building the agentic operating system that powers AI deployment across the world's most important organizations. The Platform PM is the person who determines what that foundation needs to be — and holds the bar on how well it gets built.

This is not a roadmap PM, a program manager, or a feature tracker. The Platform PM owns the core infrastructure that every FD team builds on top of: defining the foundation before anything else can be built reliably, sequencing work against real customer commitments and FD team velocity, identifying which FD-built patterns are ready to graduate to core, and ensuring that every capability that ships does so at a bar customers can trust without thinking about it.

The best Platform PMs have defined platform capabilities at production bar in high-stakes environments and understand the difference between what is necessary to build, what is interesting to build, and what should never be built at all.

What You'll Do

  • Define the foundation. Determine what needs to be true at the core platform layer — across each capability pillar — before anything reliable can be built on top of it.
  • Sequence it. Prioritize and order platform work given customer commitments, FD team velocity needs, and what is actually blocking progress today. Getting this wrong means building on an unstable base or building the right things in the wrong order and paying for it in rework and FD team drag.
  • Identify patterns and graduate capabilities. Watch what FD teams are building across the application layer, determine what is genuinely repeating, and make the call on what moves to core — and when. Do not rush graduation or delay it out of caution.
  • Hold the quality bar. Every capability on the platform roadmap earns its place twice: once by being necessary, and again by being done well enough that customers trust it without thinking about it. Keep the platform from becoming a graveyard of half-built capabilities.
  • Unlock delivery team time to value. Forward deployed delivery teams should spend their time solving the hardest customer problems, not rebuilding plumbing on every engagement. That requires a platform that is secure by default, deployable anywhere, observable in production, and equipped with the agentic primitives, eval infrastructure, expert judgment capture, and data reasoning capabilities that every agent workload needs.
  • Partner across the organization. Work closely with platform engineering, forward deployed PMs, and BU leads to surface signal, resolve sequencing tradeoffs, and keep the roadmap grounded in what is actually blocking work.

What We're Looking For

Must-Have Qualifications

  • 6+ years in product management with meaningful time owning platform, infrastructure, or developer-facing products at production bar.

About Scale

Scale builds AI systems for decisions that matter. We started out providing the data and evaluation behind many of the world's leading models, and we still work with the major frontier labs on research and post-training. Today we also build full applications: we take an organisation's own data and expertise, forward deploy alongside their teams, and build the systems they come to rely on, powered by the Scale GenAI Platform.

The Role

The UK is making a wholesale shift to AI. The government's AI Opportunities Action Plan set out to "mainline AI into the veins" of the country, and the focus has now moved to delivery: the Incubator for AI (i.AI) is shipping tools like the Humphrey suite into departments, a Sovereign AI Unit and AI Growth Zones are being stood up, and civilian departments are under real pressure to move from pilots to production. Scale Labs, Research Scientist — Agent Robustness

As the leading data and evaluation partner for frontier AI companies, Scale plays an integral role in understanding the capabilities and safeguarding AI models and systems. Building on this expertise, Scale Labs has launched a new team focused on policy research, to bridge the gap between AI research and global policymakers to make informed, scientific decisions about AI risks and capabilities.

Our research tackles the hardest problems in agent robustness, AI control protocols, and AI risk evaluations to help governments, industry, and the public understand and mitigate AI risk while maximizing AI adoption. This team collaborates broadly across industry, the public sector, and academia and regularly publishes our findings. We are actively seeking talented researchers to join us in shaping this vision.

As a Research Scientist working on Agent Robustness you will work on the fundamental challenges of building AI agents that are safe and aligned with humans. For example, you might:

  • Research the science of AI agent capabilities with a focus on how they relate to safety, risk factors, and methodologies for benchmarking them;
  • Design and build harnesses to test AI agents’ tendency to take harmful actions when pressured to do so by users or tricked into doing so by elements of their environment;
  • Design and build exploits and mitigations for new and unique failure modes that arise as AI agents gain affordances like coding, web browsing, and computer use;
  • Characterize and design mitigations for potential failure modes or broader risks of systems involving multiple interacting AI agents.

Ideally you’d have:

jobs.title: Safety Research Scholar - Human Frontier Labs
jobs.description:
About the Program

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with Scale Labs, we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety.

That work includes finding where models fail, checking whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Scholars take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded.

Each scholar owns a substantial part of a safety research project. You'll work alongside a mentor from the research question through the experiments to deciding what to test next.

Research Areas

Mentors will guide Research Scholars on projects in selected AI safety research areas in select AI safety research areas, such as:

  • AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AIs, including detecting harmful intent or deception.
  • Alignment auditing and evaluations: Building scalable methods to test whether models have hidden goals, misaligned behaviors or unsafe tendencies.
  • Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior.
  • Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) safety: Investigating how to keep AI systems safe and aligned as AIs increasingly contribute to their own development.
  • Science of Evaluations: examining when and how models recognize they're being tested, and how situational awareness affects the reliability/validity of evaluations.
  • Misuse risks and evaluations: Developing methods to assess how AI systems could be exploited by malicious actors, including evaluating their potential to enable harmful activities.

Projects are matched to demonstrated expertise; we don’t expect any candidate to cover every area.

Representative Research

  • ASPI: 728 task–attack scenarios testing how clarification-seeking changes prompt-injection vulnerability in LLM agents.
  • PropensityBench: simulating real-world pressure to choose between safe or harmful behavior
  • BioRiskEval: evaluating whether safeguards for open-weight bio-foundation models remain robust under fine-tuning and probing.
  • See more work from the Human Frontier Collective.

Our senior machine learning engineers are handed problems that don't yet have an established approach, they propose the architecture, build it with support from other engineers, and are accountable for whether it holds up in the environments our customers depend on.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with our primary focus on agentic systems built on large language models. We are developing agents that solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners: agent frameworks that integrate custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, memory and context-management systems that hold state across long-running tasks, geospatial reasoning over maps and spatial data, and the evaluation tooling that benchmarks and refines agent behavior. We also apply reinforcement learning in targeted places where it earns its keep, and our computer vision work advances evaluation, labeling efficiency, and multimodal model training in support of defense applications.

As a Senior MLE, you'll have design authority over a capability area - the final say on the patterns used within your team, and the responsibility to make those patterns work under real constraints: classified environments, limited compute, and correctness requirements that don't bend.

  • Define net-new patterns in problem spaces with no established approach, propose them to the wider team, and lead the work to build them
  • Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community and put them into production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
  • Improve and maintain production models and agents through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics

As a Senior Software Engineer, AI Ops at Scale AI, you will own the long-term technical health, performance, and stability of AI solutions deployed across our strategic public sector partners.

While our Delivery Teams build and launch new use cases, you are the technical steward ensuring these deployments operate with Operational Excellence. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Orchestration Platform
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA; New York, NY
jobs.description:
Scale is building reliable AI systems for the world’s most important decisions. Our products help leading enterprises, governments, and frontier AI labs build, deploy, and evaluate AI systems at scale.

The Orchestration Platform is a core technology used across the company to run durable, reliable, and scalable workflows. It powers the complex, long-running processes behind Scale’s products - from data and model-evaluation pipelines to operational systems and customer-facing workflows.

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will help build and evolve this foundational orchestration platform. You will design the primitives, services, and developer experience that enable teams across Scale to author, operate, observe, and safely scale distributed workflows. This is a high-leverage role for an engineer excited by distributed systems, reliability, and platform infrastructure used by many internal teams.

You will:

  • Lead the architecture, design, implementation, and operation of Scale’s core orchestration platform.
  • Build durable workflow infrastructure using technologies such as Temporal, Cadence, Kubernetes, and cloud-native systems.
  • Define platform primitives and APIs for scheduling, retries, state management, task execution, observability, and workflow lifecycle management.
  • Partner with product, infrastructure, data, and application teams to understand workflow needs and turn them into reusable platform capabilities.
  • Improve the reliability, scalability, security, and developer experience of services that run critical company workflows.
  • Establish technical standards and best practices for distributed workflow development, deployment, testing, and incident response.
  • Drive cross-functional technical decisions and communicate platform direction clearly to engineers and stakeholders.

Ideally, you have:

  • 5+ years of full-time software engineering experience, with a focus on backend, infrastructure, and distributed systems.
  • Experience building and operating production systems with strong requirements for reliability, availability, and scale.
  • Deep familiarity with workflow orchestration platforms such as Temporal, Cadence, AWS Step Functions, Kubernetes, or similar systems.
  • Deep familiarity with Kubernetes and containerized production environments, and familiarity with Terraform, Docker.
  • Strong knowledge of distributed-systems concepts, including asynchronous execution, retries, idempotency, fault tolerance, state management, and observability.
  • A track record of leading technically complex projects from design through rollout and ongoing operation.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively with platform consumers and non-technical stakeholders.

Nices to haves:

  • Experience with data warehouses (Snowflake, Firebolt) and data pipeline/ETL

jobs.description:
About Scale AI

At Scale, our mission is to develop reliable AI systems for the world's most important decisions. Our products provide the high-quality data and full-stack technologies that power the world's leading models, and help enterprises and governments build, deploy, and oversee AI applications that deliver real impact.

Scale Frontier Data is the organization behind the training and evaluation data that frontier labs depend on. We build the systems, tooling, and expert workflows that turn hard human expertise into signals that models can learn from, across reasoning, coding, agentic tool use, and domain expertise.

Reinforcement learning environments are now the center of gravity for that work: the difference between a model that demos well and a model that reliably completes long-horizon work is almost always the quality of the environments and reward signals it was trained against.

Responsibilities

As a Staff Software Engineer, RL Environments, you'll own the technical foundation for how Scale builds, runs, verifies, and delivers RL environments at scale.

An RL environment is a real piece of software: a containerized world with real dependencies, real state, real tools, and a grader that has to be correct even when the agent is creative about breaking it. Building one is a full-stack engineering problem. Building thousands of them reproducibly, cheaply, with trustworthy reward signals and throughput measured in millions of rollouts is a systems problem that very few people have solved.

You'll work on both. You'll design the platform: sandboxed execution, environment packaging and versioning, rollout orchestration, trajectory capture, verifier frameworks, and the authoring surfaces that let engineers and domain experts produce environments without reinventing infrastructure each time. And you'll go deep on the environments themselves by instrumenting real applications, designing task suites that expose specific capability gaps, and building graders that hold up under adversarial optimization.

This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll set technical direction across multiple teams, and you'll still be the person who writes the hard part.

Required Qualifications

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience with strong fundamentals in distributed systems, system design, data structures, and algorithms.
  • Strong Python skills and a track record of shipping production software; comfort in at least one other part of the stack (TypeScript/React, Go, Rust, or similar).
  • Deep experience with containerization and sandboxed execution, including Docker, VMs, gVisor/Firecracker, Kubernetes, or equivalent.
  • Experience building or operating high-throughput backend systems: orchestration, job scheduling, queuing, and large-scale data pipelines.

jobs.title: Sr. Product Manager (Epic Online Services)
jobs.description:
WHAT MAKES US EPIC?

At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.

Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.

PRODUCT MANAGEMENT

What We Do

Product Management partners with game development, publishing, marketing, and platform teams to provide a data and market-driven view of product strategy that aligns with business goals. As part of Epic’s Growth Team, we use our product expertise to identify and drive growth levers to grow our player base and business.

What You'll Do

As a Senior Product Manager on the Epic Online Services team, you will lead a core set of the social and identity features that help players establish who they are and connect with others across mobile, PC, and console. You'll focus on the foundational systems behind player profiles, friends, presence, and cross-platform continuity, and be accountable for whether each release measurably improves adoption, engagement, and retention. You'll work with Design, Engineering, Production, and partner teams to plan, ship, measure, and refine features within the platform roadmap.

In this role, you will

  • Own the roadmap and performance of a defined set of social and identity features (such as profiles, friends, presence, communication, or account continuity), contributing to the unified platform strategy
  • Lead the end-to-end user experience of these features, and use data and experimentation to evaluate feature performance and identify opportunities to improve adoption, engagement, and retention
  • Partner with Engineering to deliver scalable, high-performance systems that support social and identity features for millions of players globally, balancing usability, performance, privacy, and scalability
  • Define clear goals and success metrics for each feature and release, and hold the work accountable to them
  • Lead product reviews and internal tests on launches, and turn findings into clear recommendations for future planning
  • Identify gaps in our social and identity toolkit and make the case for new features or improvements where the data supports it

What we're looking for

  • Product management experience on consumer-facing platform products or shared systems, preferably on social and/or identity features
  • Proven track record delivering social and/or identity platform features, and measurably improving their performance
  • Strong analytic

jobs.title: Producer - Star Trek Fleet Command
jobs.description:
Scopely is looking for a Producer to join our Star Trek Fleet Command game in London on a hybrid basis.

At Scopely, we care deeply about what we do and want to inspire play, every day - whether in our work environments alongside our talented colleagues, or through our deep connections with our communities of players. We are a global team of game lovers who are developing, publishing and innovating the mobile games industry, connecting millions of people around the world daily.

Star Trek Fleet Command's ongoing success goes from strength to strength. Our in-house developed 4X MMO was launched in 2018 and continues to evolve, being consistently one of the top 10 gross revenue Massive Multiplayer Strategy games on the market.

What You Will Do

The person in this position will join an experienced team of producers dedicated to facilitating multi-disciplined pods to deliver the best for our players by creating and improving communication channels, celebrating successes, and always making sure we understand how and where our teams can improve.

You will be embedded in one of our pods to deliver a wide variety of updates and capabilities for Star Trek™ Fleet Command, taking these projects from concept to delivery. We work on exciting products and games and you will have the opportunity to make a massive impact on the daily experiences of hundreds of thousands of players by ensuring your team has everything they need to be successful.

  • Be heavily involved in production, coordination, triage, and release planning
  • Work directly with talented multi-disciplined feature/content teams to drive the best output and healthy team cultures
  • Facilitate requirement gathering, identifying dependencies, and capacity planning within the team, partnering with the product team, the art team, as well as the wider senior game leadership team
  • Maintain project status and progress so you can ensure teams capability to deliver to the player on time
  • Maintain and iterate on team processes such as retrospectives and sprint planning to keep the team healthy and contributing to the overall improvement of the studio
  • Be an active member of the Star Trek Fleet Command production team to improve how the whole game team operates

What We're Looking For

  • 3+ years of production experience in development teams
  • Experience on a live title
  • Excellent communication and people interaction skills
  • Solid understanding of Agile and its standard practices
  • Experience working with JIRA
  • Naturally be a very structured and well organized person
  • Clear ability to assess priority of multiple issues rapidly to focus response accordingly
  • To have a demonstrated ability to facilitate cross team discussion and organization
  • Willing to spend a lot of time in the details of how games are delivered

Nabla delivers a unified clinical AI platform used by healthcare organizations across specialties and care settings. The platform includes:

Ambient AI documentation  that captures clinical conversations and generates structured notes.

AI-powered dictation and clinical workflow tools  embedded directly within EHR systems.

Agentic AI capabilities  that support multi-step clinical and administrative tasks.

Enterprise-grade infrastructure  built for secure deployment across health systems.

The best of AI at the service of healthcare

Nabla’s phenomenal traction is the result of 3 years of diligent product development.  Led by former Meta AI Research engineers, our team has consistently anticipated how AI can revolutionize healthcare delivery. Yann LeCun, Meta’s ex-Chief AI Scientist and Turing award winner, is an advisor to Nabla. He’s now focused on AMI Labs, with whom we have a close partnership.

Your team  At Nabla, product development is led jointly by Engineering and Product and organized into cross-functional squads, each focused on a specific product area. Squads bring together product managers, designers, engineers of different profiles, and domain experts, and operate with a high level of ownership.  As a Full-stack Engineer, you'll join one of these squads and contribute end to end to a specific part of the product.

Real-time audio transcription:  capturing and streaming audio reliably, from in-person visits as well as video consultations, and turning it into transcripts with very low latency

Resilience:  keeping the product working on weak or unstable networks, with no data lost and no disruption to the clinician

Complex AI services:  designing and running multi-stage LLM pipelines and agentic workflows at scale, with the reliability and auditability a clinical setting requires

These challenges come with demanding product requirement s:

Zero friction:  clinicians have no time to learn a new tool, so the product must be fast to set up, intuitive, and useful from the very first consultation

Trust:  what we generate goes into patient records, so quality and reliability are non-negotiable

Works everywhere:  web, desktop and mob

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the leader of Partner Services Delivery and Success within Partnerships at Anthropic, you will lead the global field delivery, partner success and partner health teams that make Claude deployments succeed at our customers when our partners build and run them. This is a senior leadership role on the Partnerships leadership team, reporting to the Global Head of Partnerships.

A deployment starts with work the business wants an agent to do: a research process in a bank, claims handling at an insurer, engineering workflows in a retailer. A partner's engineers build it against the customer's own systems and data, evaluate it on real work rather than a demo, and put it live. If it holds, the customer builds the next ten themselves and the partner carries the pattern to the next customer in that industry.

What good means is the same every time, whoever builds it: on time, on track, high quality, high customer satisfaction, and impact the customer can see in their own business. Holding that across thousands of deployments a year, almost none of which your own people build, is the job.

This is a build, and it is a scaling problem. The function is new, the teams are mostly still to be hired, demand is growing far faster than any team can be hired against it, and the way we deploy agents is changing faster than a method written down in advance can keep up with.

What you will own

  • Deployment strategy and approached. Bringing the best ways to deploy Claude to our customers through partners: which deployment approaches we back, which partners we build them with, and how both change as the models and the use cases move.
  • Field delivery. A global organisation across the Americas and international markets, which you hire, lead and grow. Our own people, in region, alongside the partner's team on live engagements: they run the delivery cadence, hold the work to date and quality, and are the first to know when something is going wrong. jobs.title: Senior Level Designer - Stumble Guys!
jobs.description:
Scopely is seeking a Senior Level Designer to join our Stumble Guys team!

Stumble Guys is one of our most recent hits, with millions of fans joining the party every day and keeping the game at the top of the charts in more than 50 countries. Our ambition is to build a beloved franchise that players enjoy for many years to come.
This is a key role within the Gameplay team. As a Senior Level Designer, you will help shape the moment-to-moment player experience by designing levels, objectives, rules, and gameplay systems that are fun, readable, scalable, and replayable. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to create experiences that are accessible to new players while offering depth and mastery for returning players around the world.

What You Will Do

  • Design and iterate on levels, courses, arenas, objectives, and interactive gameplay spaces across a range of game modes.
  • Develop new win conditions, objectives, and progression structures that create varied and engaging multiplayer experiences.
  • Design and adapt gameplay rules to support different player capabilities, interaction styles, and gameplay strategies.
  • Explore how levels, objectives, rules, and player abilities work together to create clear, exciting, and replayable experiences.
  • Create gameplay experiences that accommodate different player skill levels while maintaining competitive integrity and a strong sense of fun.
  • Write clear design documentation, including level-design briefs, gameplay rules, feature specifications, implementation guidelines, and iteration notes.
  • Prototype, block out, and iterate on levels and gameplay systems using appropriate in-game tools and workflows.
  • Collaborate closely with Engineering, Art, UX/UI, Production, Product Analytics, QA, Audio, Community, and other designers to bring features from concept to release.
  • Use playtests, player feedback, telemetry, and live data to identify opportunities and improve level flow, pacing, difficulty, clarity, and engagement.
  • Help define and maintain standards for level readability, player guidance, pacing, difficulty curves, fairness, and accessibility.
  • Partner with other designers to ensure that new gameplay systems integrate effectively across levels, modes, and player experiences.

What We're Looking For

  • Significant professional experience in level design, gameplay design, or a related discipline, ideally in multiplayer or live-service games.
  • A strong portfolio demonstrating shipped levels, game modes, objectives, or multiplayer gameplay experiences.
  • Strong understanding of level-design fundamentals, including layout, flow, pacing, spatial composition, player guidance, difficulty, readability, and replayability.
  • Experience developing level-design guidelines, standards, and documentation that can be adopted by a broader team.

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.  We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.  Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.  Guided by our five values  Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship,  culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.  Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

WHO YOU ARE

You are a commercial leader who has built the go-to-market of a platform from a blank page and knows what it takes to turn a product that people already use into a business that pays for itself. You have priced and packaged products for marketplaces, brands or merchants, and you have seen the difference between a model that looks good in a spreadsheet and one that a small business owner actually adopts.  You are comfortable in a B2B2C world: the customer is reached through someone else's channel, the data belongs to the ecosystem, and the money comes from several ends of a transaction at once. You influence without authority, because the teams that execute will rarely report to you. You are rigorous with numbers and plain with people, and you are at ease saying what the evidence shows even when the room expects something else.  You want to build something that reaches millions of small businesses, you are prepared to work for it.

And beyond.  ⭐  SECURITY ASSOCIATE INTERNSHIP  ⭐  Six-month end-of-studies internship in Paris.  Looking for an end-of-studies internship where you do real cybersecurity work, not a side project nobody uses? Automate what repeats , so the team spends its time where the risk is

Owned a recurring security campaign end to end and left it cheaper for the next round

Written your end-of-studies thesis on a real security subject

Our entrepreneurial spirit drives us in what we do and what we are passionate about. Our mission is to become the premier health partner in the insurance business. Our data and tech give us an edge in risk assessment, pricing and premium calculation. jobs.description:

If you've built something before, start here  The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.  What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera  Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.

What you'll do  You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.

Spend real time with customers.  Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

Shape what to build.  Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

Build it.  Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

Ship, then check.  Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

Own it in production.  When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

Build with AI.  Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

What success looks like after 3 months

There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

You'll probably thrive here if

You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

You've built and run backend systems in product

jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
jobs.description:
This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations.

If you've built something before, start here  Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.  We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera  Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

What you'll own  You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

Training and fine-tuning : embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

Document understanding : models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

Product matching : retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

Evaluation : offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

Training and serving infrastructure : automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

Customer problems : when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

What success looks like after 3 months

There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next.

You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD

You’ll turn each program launch into a major market moment, celebrate milestones like new cohorts and the first badges earned, and build a community of graduates who help tell the story.

Because the Academy serves both partners and customers, this role will sit on our Partner Marketing team. You’ll work directly with partners and customers to secure their participation in announcements and bring them into our launch and amplification plans. You’ll help shape the Academy’s strategy and annual plan and represent marketing with senior leaders, while staying hands-on enough to write the first draft yourself. Partners and customers already engage with other Anthropic education and training programs, so you’ll be thoughtful about how the Academy fits alongside them. If you’ve built a branded program at a B2B technology company and want to do it again at a much bigger scale, this role is for you.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the marketing strategy and annual plan for Claude Frontier Academy and its programs, working with Academy leadership to set priorities and goals

  • Build and maintain a calendar of market moments for the Academy and each program, including program launches, new cohorts, and badge milestones

  • Lead launches end to end, from messaging and announcement drafts through legal and executive review, launch-day execution and post-launch amplification

  • Partner with Communications on press releases and announcements, including sourcing customer and partner quotes and securing approval to use their names

  • Align early with Partnerships, Communications, and Account Teams on which customers and partners are named in each announcement, who gets a heads-up before it goes

jobs.title: Chief Marketing Officer, Factor Europe

Factor is the #1 ready-to-eat brand for people who see personal health as a key ingredient to achieving their goals. Developed by chefs and dietitians, Factor makes healthy eating effortless, enjoyable, and full of flavor. Part of the HelloFresh Group, Factor is the fastest-growing business in the group, and we are now building the next chapter in Europe.
